paper.title: Maximizing the spread of influence through a social network

headline: KKT 2003 IC + influence-max (hybrid): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; P1 crossing lambda=1.12 (sub=0.000, super=0.577); P2 submodular 1.000; P3 greedy/OPT=0.996, greedy>7.4 random

verdicts.gate: P1 percolation transition: mean reached < 0.05 @ lambda=0.5, > 0.40 @ lambda=2.0, crossing in [0.8,1.3]
P2 influence spread is submodular: marginal gain(A) >= marginal gain(B) for nested A subset B in >=95% of pairs
P3 greedy attains 1-1/e: sigma(greedy) >= 0.632*sigma(OPT) for k=3 AND greedy > random

extra.framing: HYBRID (disclosed): agent activation state on abm_auto._platform + edge-probability single-shot cascade + combinatorial optimization gate (greedy/CELF/brute-force OPT)
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model (no real-world data); the contribution is whether the harness + lock-first discipline reproduce the IC percolation transition, the exact submodularity of the influence function, and the greedy 1-1/e guarantee — and would catch an artifact. The submodularity gate is the discriminating property that separates IC from the node-threshold cascade models already built (watts/granovetter/complex-contagion), which lack it.

citations: Kempe, D., Kleinberg, J. & Tardos, E. (2003). Maximizing the spread of influence through a social network. Proc. 9th ACM SIGKDD (KDD '03):137-146. doi:10.1145/956750.956769.
Goldenberg, J., Libai, B. & Muller, E. (2001). Talk of the network: A complex systems look at the underlying process of word-of-mouth. Marketing Letters 12(3):211-223.
Leskovec, J. et al. (2007). Cost-effective outbreak detection in networks (CELF). Proc. 13th ACM SIGKDD:420-429.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the percolation transition, the submodularity fraction, and the greedy/OPT ratio
